summary: This document specifies how to encode Multipoint LDP (mLDP) Forwarding Equivalence Classes in the NLRI of BGP MCAST-VPN routes. This supports multicast in BGP/MPLS IP VPN services when mLDP provides the provider tunnels.

eli5.summary: Providers carry customers' group broadcasts across their network. This document defines the exact format of the note that tells the network which tunnel to use.

why was rfc 6514 updated for mldp

how is an mldp fec encoded in nlri
subtitle: A new BGP route format so customers using mLDP multicast can be carried across a provider's MPLS VPN.

tldr.problem: RFC 6514 can carry a customer's mLDP multicast state in BGP only under restrictive assumptions: no PIM/IGMP in the same VPN, only P2MP trees, and only 32-bit or 128-bit opaque values.
tldr.mechanism: Three new MCAST-VPN route types carry a complete mLDP FEC Element in the NLRI in place of the multicast source and group fields. They get their own codepoint range, 0x43 to 0x7f.
tldr.outcome: A provider can support customers that use mLDP in any way, with the same procedures as the matching RFC 6514 routes. The RFC updates RFC 6514.

today: RFC 7441 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6514. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Many service providers offer BGP/MPLS IP VPN service. When a customer has IP multicast traffic in its VPN, the provider must signal the customer's multicast state across its backbone. RFC 6514 does this with Multiprotocol BGP updates whose SAFI is MCAST-VPN. The NLRI carries a customer multicast source and group, so the (S,G) or (*,G) state of PIM and IGMP can be expressed.

Some customers use MPLS multicast instead, or as well. This document covers customers who use mLDP to build Point-to-Multipoint (P2MP) and Multipoint-to-Multipoint (MP2MP) Label Switched Paths. Their state is named by an mLDP FEC Element, not by (S,G). Other MPLS multicast control protocols are out of scope.

The same procedures can be combined with the global table multicast work to serve customers that use MPLS multicast outside a VPN.
sections.eli5: Some customers describe the groups they want in a different way than the old system expected. This document teaches the provider's network to understand that second way.

sections.title: Why the Old Encoding Falls Short
sections.content:
An mLDP FEC Element has a FEC Type, a Root Node and an Opaque Value. RFC 6514 squeezed it into the NLRI by putting the Root Node in the Multicast Source field and the Opaque Value in the Multicast Group field. That only works when all three of these hold:

  1. The customer does not also use PIM/IGMP. A receiver cannot tell whether the group field holds an IP address or an opaque value.
  2. The customer uses only the P2MP FEC Element, not MP2MP, because the old encoding has no way to carry the FEC type.
  3. The customer uses only opaque values exactly 32 or 128 bits long. Other lengths are declared out of scope, and mLDP has many opaque value types besides the Generic LSP Identifier.

This document removes those conditions.
sections.eli5: The old note had a small box that only fit certain kinds of answers. If you used a different kind, it got confused.

sections.title: Three New Route Types
sections.content:
RFC 6514 expects an mLDP FEC Element in three MCAST-VPN route types: the C-multicast Source Tree Join route, the S-PMSI A-D route and the Leaf A-D route. The other four types never need one. The Shared Tree Join and Source Active A-D routes describe unidirectional shared trees, which mLDP does not have. The two I-PMSI A-D routes do not name specific customer multicast state.

This document defines a twin of each of the three: the C-Multicast Source Tree Join route for C-multicast mLDP, the S-PMSI A-D route for C-multicast mLDP and the Leaf A-D route for C-multicast mLDP. Each has its own route type, and the procedures of the matching RFC 6514 route generally apply to it.

A receiver that sees an unrecognized route type follows the typed NLRI rule of the BGP error handling draft and discards the route.
sections.eli5: Instead of stretching the old forms, the document adds three new forms, each a copy of an old one with a roomier box for the answer.

sections.title: How the NLRI Is Built
sections.content:
In each new route the Multicast Source Length, Multicast Source, Multicast Group Length and Multicast Group fields are removed. One whole mLDP FEC Element, as defined in RFC 6388, takes their place. That gives:

  • S-PMSI A-D route: Route Distinguisher, mLDP FEC, Originating Router's IP Address.
  • Source Tree Join route: Route Distinguisher, Source AS, mLDP FEC.
  • Leaf A-D route derived from an S-PMSI A-D route: the Route Key stays the NLRI of that route.
  • Other Leaf A-D routes: Route Distinguisher, mLDP FEC Element, Ingress PE router IP address.

The FEC Element has an address family field for its Root Node Address. It MUST correspond to the AFI of the BGP update. Corresponding means identical values, or the update's AFI is IPv4 and the FEC says Multi-Topology IPv4, or the AFI is IPv6 and the FEC says Multi-Topology IPv6.

Wildcards in S-PMSI A-D routes are defined only for PIM customers. Their use with mLDP is outside this document.
sections.eli5: The old small boxes are thrown out and one big box holds the full description of the tunnel. The tunnel's address type must match the type the message says it uses.

sections.title: The New Route Types Registry
sections.content:
RFC 6514 created no registry for MCAST-VPN route types. IANA created "BGP MCAST-VPN Route Types" under the BGP Parameters registry, with the allocation policy Standards Action. It has three ranges: 0x01-0x3f for Generic/PIM routes, 0x43-0x7f for the mLDP range, and 0x80-0xff reserved.

The new types have the high-order two bits 0x01 and the same low-order six bits as the type they mirror. So requests should ask for two codepoints at once, one in each range, marking an unneeded one "Reserved".
sections.eli5: Each new form gets a number that looks like its older twin's number, with a special marker added, so the pairs are easy to match.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document only specifies how to encode an mLDP FEC Element in some of the BGP updates defined in RFC 6514. The security considerations of mLDP (RFC 6388) and of RFC 6514 apply, and the RFC says no new security considerations are raised.
sections.eli5: The new notes do not add new dangers. The same safety rules as before still apply.
